key_insight: The paper shows that humanoid robots can be designed to be safer for humans by optimizing both the robot’s body and its motion together. In ergoCub, this shared embodied intelligence approach reduced human back stress while also improving walking robustness.
problem_solved: Traditional humanoid robot design often optimizes performance without fully accounting for human safety and physical strain during interaction. This work addresses the challenge of building robots that are both capable and human-aware, especially in terms of minimizing spinal load during locomotion and interaction.
method: Co-optimized robot hardware and motion control using a shared embodied intelligence framework.
Included human-centered metrics, such as back stress/spinal load, alongside locomotion performance objectives.
Developed and tested the ergoCub humanoid robot to evaluate safety, robustness, and walking behavior in realistic scenarios.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper highlights a practical path toward human-aware embodied AI: not just making robots move well, but making them safer and more cooperative around people. It is especially relevant for robotics, reinforcement learning, and human-robot interaction research where optimization must balance task success with human well-being.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of standard humanoid optimization vs. shared embodied intelligence with human-aware metrics
Annotated ergoCub robot schematic showing hardware and control components
Before/after chart comparing spinal load or back stress during locomotion
Robustness or walking stability plot showing performance improvements across conditions
paper_title: Towards shared embodied intelligence in humanoid robots through optimization, development and testing of the human-aware ergoCub robot
paper_authors: Carlotta Sartore, Mohamed Elobaid, Lorenzo Rapetti, Giulio Romualdi, Stefano Dafarra
